newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavarian premier speaks out again on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Bavarian premier speaks out again on EMU.

text.p: Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber on Friday restated his commitment to a strict interpretation of the entry criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) and said a delay to the project would not lead to chaos.

Stoiber, who has warned in a flurry of interviews over the past few days against any leniency when it comes to choosing the candidates for EMU, said the budget deficit ceiling for members must be 3.0 percent of gross domestic product.
"If we said 3.2 or 3.4, then others would start to talk about 3.8 or 4.2," he said in an interview with Friday's edition of the Die Welt daily, distributed in advance to media organisations.

Asked what would happen if the EMU start date of January 1, 1999 were to be postponed, Stoiber said: "It certainly won't lead to the chaos people claim. The aim won't be abandoned. We'll come to a new agreement and a temporary solution."
His comments contrasted sharply with remarks by Chancellor Helmut Kohl to parliament earlier on Thursday.
"Those who want to delay the introduction of the euro should know that this could possibly be a permanent delay," Kohl said. "We cannot afford this."
The Bavarian premier is a senior member of the Christian Social Union, sister party to Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU). Together they form a coalition with the Free Democrats in Bonn.
